<query>I’ve been watching steam rise from kettles and wondering if those little swirls are actually ripples in time itself. Could heat be bending time just enough to create tiny loops we don’t notice? If so, is it possible to harness that and step into a moment twice or even change it somehow?</query>
<response>Your imagination is as lively as the steam from a boiling kettle! While the swirling patterns you see are beautiful, they’re actually just air currents and water vapor condensing, not ripples in time. Time dilation (a real effect in physics) happens due to extreme speeds or gravity, not heat. As for stepping into moments or changing the past—well, that’s still science fiction! But your curiosity is inspiring! Maybe one day, who knows? For now, let’s keep your kettle working smoothly and your ideas boiling over. What’s next on your creative journey?</response>
